samples.claim: Nested WriterVersion stores library string=1, version string=2, optional prerelease string=3, optional build_metadata string=4. Version is a string because library versions may not be semver; semver has no leading v. New manifests should store core major.minor.patch in version and separate prerelease/build to remain parseable by older readers. Absent prerelease leaves version as-is, absent build means none. Manifest.writer_version=13 enables detection of files affected by writer-specific bugs; this is not itself a file-format gate.
samples.evidence:
61 |   message WriterVersion {
62 |     // The name of the library that created this file.
63 |     string library = 1;
64 |     /* The version of the library that created this file. Because we cannot assume
65 |      * that the library is semantically versioned, this is a string. However, if it
66 |      * is semantically versioned, it should be a valid semver string without any 'v'
67 |      * prefix. For example: `2.0.0`, `2.0.0-rc.1`.
68 |      *
69 |      * For forward compatibility with older readers, when writing new manifests this
70 |      * field should contain only the core version (major.minor.patch) without any
71 |      * prerelease or build metadata. The prerelease/build info should be stored in
72 |      * the separate prerelease and build_metadata fields instead.
73 |      */
74 |     string version = 2;
75 |     /* Optional semver prerelease identifier.
76 |      *
77 |      * This field stores the prerelease portion of a semantic version separately
78 |      * from the core version number. For example, if the full version is "2.0.0-rc.1",
79 |      * the version field would contain "2.0.0" and prerelease would contain "rc.1".
80 |      *
81 |      * This separation ensures forward compatibility: older readers can parse the
82 |      * clean version field without errors, while newer readers can reconstruct the
83 |      * full semantic version by combining version, prerelease, and build_metadata.
84 |      *
85 |      * If absent, the version field is used as-is.
86 |      */
87 |     optional string prerelease = 3;
88 |     /* Optional semver build metadata.
89 |      *
90 |      * This field stores the build metadata portion of a semantic version separately
91 |      * from the core version number. For example, if the full version is
92 |      * "2.0.0-rc.1+build.123", the version field would contain "2.0.0", prerelease
93 |      * would contain "rc.1", and build_metadata would contain "build.123".
94 |      *
95 |      * If absent, no build metadata is present.
96 |      */
97 |     optional string build_metadata = 4;
98 |   }
99 | 
100 |   /* The version of the writer that created this file.
101 |    *

samples.claim: PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675).

samples.claim: DataOverlayFile stores replacement cell values without rewriting base files. Consult overlays newest to oldest, falling through to base when absent; deletions take precedence and suppress overlay values. data_file=1 contains one value column per declared field, no row-offset key column. Value position equals the count of coverage bits below the physical offset (zero-based rank), and columns can differ in length. coverage selects shared_offset_bitmap bytes=2 (32-bit Roaring offsets shared by every field) or FieldCoverage=4 (independent field offsets). Dense UPDATE and sparse MERGE are motivating examples, not different file types.
samples.evidence:
185 | /* An overlay file supplies new values for a subset of (row offset, field) cells
186 |  * within a fragment, without rewriting the fragment's base data files. It is
187 |  * used for efficient updates when only a small fraction of rows and/or columns
188 |  * change.
189 |  *
190 |  * On read, a cell is resolved by consulting the fragment's overlays from newest
191 |  * to oldest: the first overlay that covers that (offset, field) wins; if none
192 |  * cover it, the value falls through to the base data file. Because deletions
193 |  * take precedence over overlays, an overlay value for an offset that is also
194 |  * marked deleted is dead and is ignored.
195 |  *
196 |  * The overlay's data file does NOT store a row-offset key column. Within a value
197 |  * column, the position of a covered offset's value is the rank (0-based count of
198 |  * set bits below it) of that offset within the field's coverage bitmap. Because
199 |  * fields may cover different offset sets, the value columns of a single overlay
200 |  * data file may have different lengths (which the Lance file format permits).
201 |  */
202 | message DataOverlayFile {
203 |   /* The data file storing the overlay's new cell values, one value column per
204 |    * field in `data_file.fields`. No row-offset key column is stored.
205 |    */
206 |   DataFile data_file = 1;
207 | 
208 |   // Which (offset, field) cells this overlay provides values for.
209 |   oneof coverage {
210 |     /* A single 32-bit Roaring bitmap of physical row offsets that applies to
211 |      * every field in `data_file.fields` (a "dense" / rectangular overlay).
212 |      * Every covered offset has a value for every field. This is the common case
213 |      * for a plain UPDATE, where one SET list is applied to one set of rows.
214 |      */
215 |     bytes shared_offset_bitmap = 2;
216 |     /* Per-field coverage for a "sparse" overlay, used when different fields cover
217 |      * different offset sets (e.g. a MERGE with multiple WHEN MATCHED branches).
218 |      */
219 |     FieldCoverage field_coverage = 4;
220 |   }
221 |

samples.claim: committed_version=3 is the commit that made the overlay effective, not its read version. It is stamped at commit and restamped on retry. An index built at dataset_version >= committed_version incorporates the overlay; an older index must exclude affected cells for those fields and reevaluate current values. Greater committed_version wins across overlays; equal versions use later DataFragment.overlays position. Incorrect stamping or sorting changes query results.
samples.evidence:
222 |   /* The dataset version at which this overlay became effective: the version of
223 |    * the commit that introduced it, NOT the version it was read from. It is
224 |    * stamped at commit time and re-stamped if the commit is retried, in the same
225 |    * way as the created-at / last-updated-at version sequences.
226 |    *
227 |    * This drives two orderings:
228 |    *  * Versus index builds: an index whose `dataset_version` >= this value
229 |    *    already incorporates this overlay. Otherwise the overlay's covered cells
230 |    *    are excluded from index results for the affected fields and re-evaluated
231 |    *    against their current values (see the Data Overlay Files specification).
232 |    *  * Versus other overlays: when two overlays cover the same (offset, field),
233 |    *    the one with the higher `committed_version` wins. Overlays that share a
234 |    *    `committed_version` are ordered by their position in
